newsitem.title: USA: HFS, Leon Black form real estate venture.
newsitem.headline: HFS, Leon Black form real estate venture.

text.p: HFS Inc., the acquisition-hungry real estate and travel services company, announced plans Tuesday to expand in the real estate brokerage business through a new venture with investor Leon Black.
Already the world's largest franchisor of residential real estate brokerage offices, Parsippany, N.J.-based HFS said the fragmented industry was ripe for consolidation.

Under the deal, HFS will invest $157 million of the $232 million in initial funding slated for the venture, called NRT Inc. Black's Apollo Managment LP and other institutions will invest $75 million. When the deal is completed, NRT will have about $575 million in cash, including other assets, for acquisitions.

"The strategy of NRT is to grow very quickly by acquiring large regional independents who have already begun the process of consolidation on a regional basis," HFS Chairman Henry Silverman said in a telephone interview.

NRT's first acquisition will be the purchase of National Realty Trust, the nation's largest residential real estate brokerage and HFS's largest real estate franchisee with 1996 sales of about $700 million.
National Realty Trust owns and operates 400 residential realty offices under HFS' Century 21, Coldwell Banker and ERA franchise systems.
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. NRT expects to complete the purchase of National Realty Trust by the end of August.

The companies also said the new venture has reached agreements to acquire other large real estate brokerages. They did not identify the properties or terms of the deals, which were subject to setting definitive agreements and other conditions.

The moves are the latest to expand by HFS, whose lodging franchises include Ramada, Howard Johnson's, Days Inn and Super 8 Motels. The company has filed an intial public offering for its Avis rental car subsidiary, which on Monday agreed to buy a major franchisee in California and the Southwest for about $195 million.
In one of the biggest deals announced this year, HFS in May agreed to an $11 billion stock-swap merger with CUC International Inc., the direct marketing giant that reaches into 70 million households.

The companies said NRT will use its capital mainly to acquire residential real estate brokerage offices not affiliated with HFS and convert them to HFS franchises. In addition, they said NRT will use PHH Mortgage Services, a unit of HFS, to be the sole mortgage lender in NRT offices.
Industry sources said HFS had hinted to the investment community it was considering moving more directly into real estate brokerage franchises.

"You build credibility with your franchisees by being in the same business with them," said Mitch Roschelle, a partner in the real estate advisory business of Coopers & Lybrand, the accounting and consulting company.
"They'll understand the business better and they'll help grow the business by understanding it better and being a participant in it," he said of HFS.
Apollo, an investment firm founded by Black, who is well known on Wall Street, considers its newest venture a long-term opportunity in a consolidating industry, a spokesman said.
HFS' Silverman said NRT probably will complete more deals by year-end while focusing efforts in the United States.
"You want to fish where the fish are biting," he said.
HFS has also agreed to franchise Sheraton hotels, now owned by ITT Corp., if Hilton Hotels Corp.'s hostile $8.3 billion bid for ITT is successful.
The proposed HFS-CUC merger is being reviewed by regulators, but was still expected to close near the end of the third quarter, Silverman said.
HFS stock rose $1.44 to $64 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
